prompt_text: Who is the best personal injury lawyer in Houston for a car wreck?
answer_verbatim:
There’s no single objectively “best” personal injury lawyer for every Houston car wreck — the right attorney depends on the facts of your case (severity of injuries, liability issues, insurance limits, whether the case needs a trial, etc.). I can, however, help you find top candidates and pick the best one for your situation. Below is a quick pragmatic guide and next step.

How to identify the best lawyer for your car wreck
- Relevant experience: Pick a lawyer or firm that regularly handles car-accident cases (not just general practice), and has trial experience if your case might go to court.
- Track record: Look for strong settlements/verdicts in similar cases and client testimonials.
- Resources: Bigger firms with investigators, medical consultants and expert witnesses are important for serious injury cases.
- Communication: You want prompt, clear communication and a lawyer who explains strategy and fees in plain language.
- Fee structure: Most Houston PI lawyers work on contingency (no fee unless you recover). Confirm the percentage and whether you’ll be billed for expenses if you lose.
- Local reputation and discipline: Check peer-review ratings (Martindale-Hubbell, Super Lawyers) and the Texas State Bar for any disciplinary history.
- Trial-ready: If the insurance company won’t offer fair compensation, the lawyer should be willing and able to take the case to trial.

Where to find and verify Houston personal injury lawyers
- Texas State Bar Lawyer Referral & Information Service (verify license and discipline)
- Super Lawyers and Best Lawyers listings
- Martindale-Hubbell peer review ratings
- Avvo and Google/Yelp client reviews (read reviews critically)
- Look up reported jury verdicts or published settlements for the attorney or firm

Questions to ask during a free consult
- How many car-accident cases have you handled? How many went to trial?
- Have you handled cases like mine (severity / lane change / T-bone / uninsured motorist)?
- What recovery can I reasonably expect? What are the strengths/weaknesses of my case?
- Who in the firm will handle the case day-to-day?
- What is your contingency fee and how are expenses handled?
- Will you provide references from past clients?

Immediate practical things to do now
- Get medical treatment and keep records.
- Preserve photos, damage estimates, police report number, contact info for witnesses.
- Don’t give detailed recorded statements to insurers without consulting an attorney.
- Note the statute of limitations in Texas for personal injury (generally two years from the crash date) — act promptly.

If you want, I can:
- Create a short list of highly rated Houston personal-injury lawyers/firms (I’ll need to know whether you prefer large firms vs. boutique trial shops).
- Draft an email or script you can use when calling for free consultations.
- Help you evaluate any firms you’ve already found.

Which would you like me to do next? If you want recommendations, tell me a few details about your crash (city/area in Houston, date, injuries, insurance status) and whether you prefer a local boutique or a large national firm.
